output.title: Why bounced addresses survive in a small business workflow
output.body:
If bounced addresses keep surviving in your list, the problem is usually not the bounce itself. It is the gap between where the email platform records the bounce and where your CRM or contact list still holds the address.

For a 1–10 person business, that makes this a bounded workflow decision, not a strategy project. You are choosing between three options: keep cleaning it up by hand, pay someone to do that cleanup, or connect the systems so the bounce signal updates the list automatically. The last option only makes sense if the data is already available where you can reach it.

The practical question is simple: does your email platform expose bounce data in a report, export, or API that you can actually read? If yes, you have a starting point for a narrow automation. If no, manual cleanup stays the baseline until the tool improves. No drama, just plumbing.

A sensible first step is to list the three or four tools you already use for sending email, storing contacts, and any automation layer you have. Then check whether the sender keeps bounce records somewhere you can pull from. That one check tells you whether this is a workflow to automate or a task to keep manual for now.

The survival of bounced addresses is usually a connection gap, not a reason to buy new software first.
